headline: Hello everyone! Network School is acquiring Farcaster.
gloss: Announces the acquisition and a four-step plan: enforce moderation rules, run an onchain vote, publish a social smart contract and Network Code with examples of good and bad behavior, and host meetups. Other clients remain permitted but may not use the Farcaster or Network School names for tokens or commercial projects.

headline: THE FARCASTER PRIZE
gloss: Reports 10,000+ counted votes (~94% support) and names @dylanb.eth the first Farcaster Prize recipient ($1,024 in Base USDC) for positive contributions. Prizes will fund public digital infrastructure and bootstrap an onchain economy; more will follow.

headline: $2048 FOR FARCASTER CLIENTS
deliverable: A microsite (quickstart + tutorial), an MIT-licensed repo, and a public vouch from a human who completed it: provision compute, run a Snapchain read node, and run a client that reads from it — three commands, no API keys.

headline: $2048 IN PRIZES FOR VIDEOS ON NORBERT ELIAS & CIVILITY
deliverable: A vertical 9:16 video of about 59 seconds explaining Norbert Elias's account of how manners and peer-to-peer self-restraint rebuilt large-scale cooperation — concrete enough for a viewer with no context, linking civility to wealth and physical safety.

context.headline: THE RESTORATION OF FRIEND SPEECH ($2048 PRIZE)
context.gloss: After an onchain vote (26,000+ votes, ~95% for a moderated reference client; ~271 accounts moderated; ~4% opted out), argues civility — as in high-trust Singapore — enables large-scale cooperation and a stronger digital economy.

headline: $1024 IN PRIZES FOR VIDEOS ON TIEBOUT SORTING
deliverable: A vertical 9:16 video, 59 seconds or less, explaining Tiebout sorting concretely to a viewer starting cold. AI tools allowed; AI slop is not.
references: Charles Tiebout, "A Pure Theory of Local Expenditures," Journal of Political Economy 64(5), 1956

headline: $1024 IN PRIZES FOR VIDEOS ON THE COMMUNISTIC SOCIETIES OF THE UNITED STATES
deliverable: A vertical 9:16 video, 59 seconds or less, for a viewer with no context: what Nordhoff's communities had in common, why some lasted a century while others collapsed within years, and what new communities can learn. AI tools allowed; AI slop is not.
references: Charles Nordhoff, The Communistic Societies of the United States (1875) — free on Project Gutenberg, shared by @farcaster in 0x117d527b2fad88814c97df3cd38ed56b59bb78ff

headline: Cloud Cartography: $1000 Prize
deliverable: An open-source, mobile-friendly tool that visualizes the social network among a chosen set of Farcaster users over time, with metrics shown on a slider.

headline: $1000 Prize for AI Conference Organizer
deliverable: An open-source AI slide validator that checks a deck's file format, runs deterministic checks and AI prompt checks, and shows pass or fail, with an organizer dashboard that merges accepted decks.

headline: $1000 FOR NETWORK STATE VISUALS
deliverable: Fully open-source visuals of how a network state forms, submitted as replies with the tools used and links to the raw files.
